2608.02415.title: Training-Free versus Training-Based Intent Classification in LLMs: Accuracy, Robustness, and Failure Modes
2608.02415.paper_summary: Intent classification in Large Language Models (LLMs) involves categorizing user prompts into predefined classes. For instance, given a user prompt, the system must determine whether it primarily concerns mathematics, coding, or general text processing. Such classification enables routing prompts to specialized models optimized for specific domains, improving both accuracy and computational efficiency. In this work, we conduct a systematic study comparing training-free vs training-based approaches for intent classification. For this purpose, we consider two lightweight, training-free methods based on statistics of internal representations and compare them against MLP classifiers and linear probes. Our comprehensive empirical evaluation reveals that 1) Both training-free and training-based methods saturate easy benchmarks (mathematics vs. coding vs. natural language), 2) Training-based classifiers have an advantage on harder classification tasks (e.g. Java vs Python), and 3) Training-free methods are generally more robust to mixed-intent and adversarial prompts.
2608.02415.paper_summary_zh: 意圖分類在大型語言模型（LLMs）中涉及將用戶提示分類為預定義的類別。<lb/>例如，給定一個用戶提示，系統必須確定它主要涉及數學、編碼還是一般文本處理。<lb/>這種分類能夠將提示路由到針對特定領域優化的專業模型，提高準確性和計算效率。<lb/>在這項工作中，我們進行了一項系統研究，比較無需訓練與基於訓練的意圖分類方法。<lb/>為此，我們考慮了兩種基於內部表示統計的輕量級無需訓練的方法，並將其與MLP分類器和線性探針進行比較。<lb/>我們的綜合實證評估顯示，1）無需訓練和基於訓練的方法在簡單基準（數學 vs. 編碼 vs. 自然語言）上都達到了飽和，2）基於訓練的分類器在更困難的分類任務（例如Java vs Python）上具有優勢，以及3）無需訓練的方法通常對混合意圖和對抗性提示更具穩健性。
